title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated video and fabricated social media profiles to pose as a real, named attorney. The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI deployment by a company offering a service. It occurred when bad actors used AI tools to manufacture convincing fake personas at scale, then distributed them across consumer social media platforms. The platforms themselves removed thousands of profiles only after the attorney's firm hired a third-party anti-piracy company to identify and report them, meaning no platform-side detection caught the impersonation proactively.

The harm landed on immigrants seeking legal help, a population with limited means to verify credentials and heightened vulnerability to threats involving their immigration status. Victims were moved off public platforms to WhatsApp, sent fabricated contracts, and paid through Venmo and Zelle, payment methods that offer little recourse after a transfer. The mechanism that would have caught this earlier, platform-level detection of coordinated inauthentic accounts using a real person's likeness, did not operate here without outside pressure.

What is not established is who the scammers are, whether any have been identified or charged, and whether the fraudulent funds have been recovered. The attorney's plans to contact authorities are reported, but no investigation or law enforcement action is confirmed in the available reporting.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, is being targeted by scammers using artificial intelligence to create fake videos and social media profiles in his name. The criminals are defrauding vulnerable immigrants by offering fraudulent services such as US residency assistance for $2,200 and claiming to help detainees escape immigration detention centers. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office after seeing the fake content online.

The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months, with an anti-piracy company hired by Leal's firm removing nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to contact numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send phony contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal is warning immigrants to verify service providers' identities and avoid sending money through digital payment apps, and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams.
